exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: In Cultural and Creative Arts, 'Bead Works' primarily refers to the art of:
options: Melting glass to form large window panes.
Stringing small perforated objects together to create jewelry and ornaments.
Carving large wooden statues for traditional festivals.
Weaving palm fronds into sleeping mats.
questions.explain: Beadwork is the art or craft of attaching beads to one another by stringing them onto a thread or thin wire with a sewing or beading needle to create items like necklaces, bracelets, and waist beads.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following is an unconventional, recycled material that students can easily use to produce beautiful beaded jewelry in the classroom?
questions.explain: Rolled paper (paper cut into triangular strips, glued, and rolled tightly around a toothpick) is a highly creative, unconventional material used to simulate colorful beads for jewelry.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Before small pieces of wood or bottle tops can be used effectively for bead work, what essential preparation must be done?
options: They must be boiled in hot water for a day.
They must be crushed into a fine powder.
A hole must be pierced or drilled through their center.
They must be burnt until they turn black.
questions.explain: For any object to function as a bead (whether wood, bottle tops, or seeds), it must have a central hole through which a string, thread, or wire can pass.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following natural items can be strung together to serve as beads for making rustic necklaces or bracelets?
questions.explain: Hard dried seeds (like melon or flamboyant seeds) and hollow straws can be threaded easily, making them excellent natural and unconventional materials for bead making.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: In Nigerian culture, a major traditional use of intricately crafted bead works is for:
options: Adorning royalty and signifying wealth and chieftaincy titles.
questions.explain: In many Nigerian traditions (such as Benin and Yoruba cultures), heavily beaded crowns, staffs, and garments are significant symbols of royalty, power, and high social status.
